page: Amazon Web Services r8g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration provides one thread per core, with 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory bandwidth performance, with read-only and write operations on large blocks placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The server also demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core Geekbench tests, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations, which reached 132.23 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls within the average range. In LLM inference tests, text generation using a small 135M model is weak, though text generation speeds for medium (7B) and large (70B) models rank in the strong category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8g.16xlarge offers high memory density and high-bandwidth memory access relative to its ARM64 compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and medium-to-large LLM inference tasks.
